title: What they said at the time

clips.q: We moved too far, too fast, under the pressures of the times.
clips.who: **Arthur E. Larkin Jr.**, former president of General Foods, The New York Times, Jun 11, 1972[^1]

clips.q: At General Foods, Did Success Breed Failure?
But Burger Chef was the event.
clips.who: **Arthur E. Larkin Jr.**, on his retirement, 1972[^1]

clips.q: …that was a lot of money to lose on hamburgers in three years…
clips.who: **Marylin Bender**, The New York Times, Jun 11, 1972[^1]
**The New York Times**, citing analysts, Mar 2, 1981[^2]

clips.q: …this business was not central to the long-term direction that we see for General Foods.
clips.who: **James L. Ferguson**, chairman of General Foods, Dec 1981[^3]

clips.q: We still have a lot of room for expansion and look forward to a very exciting future.
clips.who: **Jack Laughery**, chairman of Hardee’s, Nov 1982, as quoted by WRTV[^10]

clips.q: In certain markets like Indy and Terre Haute, the love affair with Burger Chef remains strong…
